questions.problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a  function such that ${\int }_{2}^{-2}\frac{1}{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-3$ and ${\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=10.$  What is the value of ${\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{-2}\frac{1}{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-3 \\ \frac{1}{4}{\int }_{2}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-3 \\ -\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-3 \\ {\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =12+10 \\  & =22.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that ${\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-4$ and ${\int }_{3}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x=7$ then what is ${\int }_{2}^{8}(5f(x)+4)\,\text{d}x?$
questions.worked_solution:
From the adjacent intervals rule, we know that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in the known information into the above gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-4)+7={\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 3={\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute the desired integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{8}(5f(x)+4)\,\text{d}x & =5{\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x+4{\int }_{2}^{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5(3)+4\cdot x\,{|}_{2}^{8} \\  & =15+4(8-2) \\  & =39.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{1}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(f(x)-6x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x-6{\int }_{-1}^{1}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =1-6\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot {x}^{2}\,{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =1-3({1}^{2}-(-1)^{2}) \\  & =1-3\cdot 0 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
